title: Signal-to-Action reliability runway + SLO pilot canvas
content:
Purpose and short problem statement:
This is a lightweight, action-focused canvas to run a 6-week cross-functional SLO pilot that converts observed signals into concrete operational changes. The goal is to create repeatable mechanics for: defining useful SLOs, instrumenting reliable signals, running short experiments to validate opt-in remediation, and capturing a handoff path for product teams to own steady-state operations.

Why this exists (context):
- We have many SLO definitions in docs but too few short, repeatable experiments that show product teams how to act when the signal degrades.
- Current on-call and incident flows are ad-hoc across Hosted API, Dedicated, and Private deployments. We need a pilot that surfaces friction and documents the minimal, high-leverage runbooks.
- This canvas is intentionally prescriptive: small scope, clear success criteria, and cross-team pairing to prevent documentation-only outcomes.

Scope (what this pilot will cover):
- Services: request-latency and model-availability signal on Hosted API routing layer + Dedicated autoscale behavior for a single ML model family (gpt-3-style reference).
- Teams: SRE (runbook/alerting, automation), Platform (routing, capacity), Serving-runtime (kernel/latency), Product-hosted-api (consumer side), Observability (dashboards + traces).
- Not in scope: infrastructure procurement for new HW, org-wide SLO rollout for every product.

Success metrics (how we will judge the pilot):
- 3 reproducible playbooks that convert a degraded signal -> a mitigation action (cache warm, route to variant, scale pool) documented and executed at least once during pilot.
- Mean time to remediate (MTTR) for pilot scenarios improves by >=30% between first and last run.
- Product team within pilot (alpha) can demonstrate ownership of one SLO for 2 continuous weeks post-pilot without SRE intervention.
- Baseline unit-econ impact: token-cost delta measured for fallback strategies and contained within project budget.

High-level timeline (6 weeks):
- Week 0 (prep, 1 week): finalize scope, select model-family, instrument signals, create dashboard mocks. Owners: Sophie (SRE lead), Priya (Platform), Carlos (Runtime). Linked tickets: JIRA-SRE-4123.
- Week 1-2 (experiment design): define 3 experiment scenarios, write minimal runbooks, implement synthetic traffic harness to replay degradation. Owners: Team pairs (SRE+Platform), (Runtime+Product).
- Week 3-4 (execute experiments): run each scenario twice under different load shapes, capture traces, metric drift, and cost. Observability to collect golden artifacts.
- Week 5 (retro + iterate): identify friction, update runbooks, create automation tickets for quick wins.
- Week 6 (hand-off + documentation): finalize 3 playbooks, training 60m session for product/ops, and create a public Confluence summary.

Roles and responsibilities (quick reference):
- SRE (Sophie): lead pilot cadence, define alerting thresholds, own MTTR metric collection and retro facilitation.
- Platform (Priya): implement routing toggles for canary fallback, create capacity throttles for Dedicated pool scale tests.
- Serving-runtime (Carlos): ensure KV cache and quantization variant endpoints are available for fallback tests, surface runtime constraints.
- Product-hosted-api (Mei): coordinate consumer-side acceptance tests and define user-acceptable latency windows.
- Observability (Liam): dashboards, trace collection, synthetic harness orchestration, and extraction of golden traces.

Experiment matrix (three canonical signals -> actions):
1) Signal: 95th pct request latency spike on Hosted API (region us-west1). Action: route 20% of traffic to lower-latency variant (quantized) + enable prefix cache. Observable outcome: 95th pct reduces by target amount, correctness regression <= 1%.
2) Signal: increased model load causing Dedicated pool queue growth. Action: temporarily increase pool scale (burst capacity config) + shed low-priority batch jobs. Observable outcome: queue length reduced, throughput maintained for high-priority routes.
3) Signal: KV cache hit-rate collapse on private deployment after deploy. Action: warm cache via synthetic prefetch + rollback to previous model shard for 1 hour. Observable outcome: cache hit-rate recovers within target window.

Minimal runbook template (each playbook will include):
- Triggering signal (metric and threshold)
- Quick-fire recovery steps (who clicks what, toggles, and approximate time-to-effect)
- Safety checks and blast-radius limits
- Post-action verification (metrics + user-visible checks)
- Owner for follow-up automation (ticket link)

Observability and measurement approach:
- Dashboards: one-page pilot dashboard per experiment with 1) traffic, 2) latency percentiles, 3) error-rate, 4) cost (token units), 5) trace-sampling link.
- Tracing: capture 5 golden traces per experiment (pre/post action) and store links in Confluence.
- Cost measurement: compute per-minute token cost delta for fallback strategy and record as part of experiment artifacts.

Communication plan:
- Weekly 30-minute sync (Mon 09:30 PT) during pilot; notes posted to Confluence and #sre-reliability-playbook.
- Mid-pilot demo (end of week 3) to an invite list of product leads + infra.
- Final handoff doc: clean playbooks + 60m recorded training session uploaded to Confluence.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: fallback causes correctness regressions. Mitigation: pre-define correctness SLO (e.g., model-answer similarity threshold) and only roll out to 10-20% traffic initially.
- Risk: automation takes longer than pilot window. Mitigation: favor manual-operator steps with precise checklists; create automation backlog ticket for follow-up.
- Risk: Too many stakeholders -> slow decisions. Mitigation: decision arbiter = Sophie, final say within pilot scope; escalate only if change impacts policy or budget.

Operational artifacts to produce by project end:
- 3 runbooks (doc links), 3 dashboard templates, synthetic traffic harness repo with two replay scenarios (link to PR), and a concise results dashboard summarizing MTTR and cost delta.

Open questions / decisions needed this week:
- Product: which model-family (gpt-style v1 vs v2) gives the clearest signal without heavy infra prep? (Owners: Mei + Carlos)
- Finance: confirm budget cap for burst autoscale tests (estimated $6k).
- Observability: retention policy for golden traces (how long to keep?).

Next immediate actions (this week):
- Sophie: create pilot epic in Jira and link tickets JIRA-SRE-4123, JIRA-PROD-631.
- Priya/Carlos: spin up a Dedicated test pool and expose routing toggle in staging.
- Liam: create dashboard skeleton and synthetic harness stub (PR referenced).
- Mei: identify 1 product endpoint to include in consumer acceptance checks.

Notes to self (informal):
- Keep the pilot deliberately small: 3 signals, 3 runbooks, single model family, 6-week runway.
- Capture failures as learning: a failed run = good data. Make a short post-run checklist for what to log.
- Linkage: this should feed into the broader SLO program repo but avoid being absorbed into bureaucracy. Pilot needs fast feedback loops.

Artifacts / links to create during pilot:
- Confluence summary page (template provided in linked_artifacts)
- Github PR for synthetic harness: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1789 (placeholder, update with final PR)
- Post-pilot retro doc with action owners and automation tickets

If you want to volunteer to run an experiment or pair on a runbook, ping me in slack @sophie (slack:#sre-reliability-playbook).

-- end canvas --
